Prefer the CC-0 bulk download over the API for the same reasons the Congress adapter does. sldu/sldl divisions are already in the registry (25 sldu + 58 sldl matched) and are where these attach; remember AZ elects one senator and TWO representatives per legislative district, so the many-to-many join is load-bearing from the first row. 2026-08-12 ROSTER SHIPPED, VOTES NOT - same split as D02. lib/sources/plural/, officeholders-04/33/34.json, tests/plural.test.ts 12 tests. Recorded rather than tidied over, because a tracker that names a branch which never existed is the kind of small untruth this column exists to prevent. Evidence: test (129 pass), lint and build all green. BUILT ON THE NIGHTLY BULK CSV, NOT THE v3 API: data.openstates.org/people/current/<st>.csv, one file per state, NO KEY AND NO LOGIN REQUIRED, verified live for az/nj/nh (200, 84KB/119KB/354KB). So PLURAL_API_KEY is NOT needed for the roster - it is for the API, which this does not touch. Data is CC-0; attribution is requested not required and is carried anyway. 620 legislators fetched. THE NEW HAMPSHIRE TRAP, and it is the at-large trap again in a different costume. Plural designates NH House districts by county and number - "Merrimack 8", "Rockingham 30" - while this repo identifiers are Census numeric codes, sldl:608. A direct join scores 0 OF 201 and does so silently. The bridge is the registry own Census-sourced LABEL, which carries the statutory designation: sldl:608 is labelled "State House District Merrimack 08". indexDivisions() keys on state|chamber|normalized-designation and designationKey() strips zero-padding so "Merrimack 08" meets "Merrimack 8". This is NOT the name-string join CLAUDE.md forbids: that rule is about joining geographic entities on colloquial names that collide across states, whereas a NH House district designation IS its statutory identity, the match is scoped to one state and one chamber, it is exact after normalization rather than fuzzy, and every miss is reported. Output is keyed on this repo OCD-IDs throughout. RESULT, and the denominator matters: AZ 90 legislators / 24 linked, NJ 120 / 21, NH 410 / 85. The apparent shortfall is the THREE-COUNTY CLIP, not a mismatch - the registry holds 16 AZ, 14 NJ and 53 NH legislative districts, and ALL OF THEM now have someone. Zero holes. The build prints held-vs-covered per state precisely so a clip is never mistaken for a broken join. MANY-TO-MANY CONFIRMED IN REAL DATA: AZ LD19 returns one senator (David Gowan) and TWO representatives (Gail Griffin, Lupe Diaz); NJ Assembly District 25 returns two Assemblymembers; NH Merrimack 07 returns two. A one-district-per-seat column would have had to drop half of them. CHAMBER TITLES ARE A PER-STATE TABLE, not derived: NJ lower chamber is the General Assembly and its members are Assemblymembers, not Representatives. A state with no entry reports rather than inventing a title, same rule as the body registry refusing to mint supervisors/commissioners/select boards. STILL MISSING: term dates (the CSV carries none - needs the API or the openstates/people YAML), and photos (Plural publishes an image URL; not shipped because it would be a hotlink of unknown licence - D20). QUOTA RECORDED 2026-08-12, branch claude/plural-quota-and-vendor-note, test (132 pass) lint build all green. Plural free tier is 500 GraphQL requests/day at 1 req/sec. THIS IS A QUOTA, NOT A TERMS RESTRICTION - it limits how we build, not whether we may, so D03 STAYS CLEARED. Item: MapLibre vector tile fix
Detail: Turbopack raw-copies maplibre-gl-worker.mjs without rewriting its import of maplibre-gl-shared.mjs, so the worker 404s and no .pbf is ever fetched. Vendor both files into public/ so the relative import resolves, then delete the raster branch.
Notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-11 - see the RESOLUTION paragraph at the end; the diagnosis before it was partly wrong and is kept for the record. NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_RASTER=1 is a workaround that contradicts CLAUDE.md line 12 and must not ship. Re-vendor on every maplibre-gl upgrade. Also widen the error filter in map-canvas.tsx - it currently swallows anything not matching /style|sprite|glyphs|tile/i, including Failed to fetch. 2026-08-11 diagnosis only, fix NOT applied. Root cause confirmed in a production build, so it is not dev-only and the earlier React Strict Mode theory is retracted: the worker script itself serves 200, but its first statement imports ./maplibre-gl-shared.mjs, which 404s - Turbopack copies the worker into /_next/static/media/ byte-identical (verified by file hash) without rewriting the specifier, while emitting the sibling content-hashed as maplibre-gl-shared.<hash>.mjs. Module evaluation fails, the Worker error event carries an empty message that MapLibre never surfaces, and 0 .pbf requests are ever made while style.json, tiles.json and sprite all return 200. Evidence: resource timing on localhost:3000 production build, pbf=0. Also landed this session: CARTO silent fallback removed - buildRasterStyle returns null without a key and the caller shows the Basemap unavailable notice rather than substituting a provider; must-not-ship note added at the top of lib/map/style.ts citing CLAUDE.md line 12; basemap style pinned to basic-v2-dark. Two things to undo when the raster branch is deleted: (1) buildRasterStyle() now sets a glyphs endpoint, which exists only so the district label layer has fonts on the raster path - the vector style defines its own glyphs, so remove it with the branch rather than carrying it over. (2) firstSymbolLayerId in lib/map/districts.ts returns undefined in raster mode because that style has no symbol layers, so the beforeId insertion is inert and the district layers simply append on top; once vector rendering is restored, verify the ordering actually works and that basemap place names draw above the district boundaries. RESOLUTION 2026-08-11: two independent root causes, not one. (1) The worker. The Turbopack-specific part of the diagnosis above was too narrow - maplibre-gl 6 locates its worker at runtime via new URL(template, import.meta.url) built from a variable, which is not the static form any bundler rewrites, so webpack fails identically. Verified empirically: next dev --webpack still yields 0 .pbf and the same MIME-type error, so the webpack escape hatch was ruled out rather than assumed. Fix is scripts/build-map-worker.mjs, an esbuild step that bundles the worker and its shared sibling into one self-contained 461 KB public/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs, wired to predev and prebuild so it regenerates on every maplibre-gl upgrade instead of drifting; the file is now gitignored and untracked, since a committed copy is exactly what goes stale. The script asserts the bundle has no unresolved imports left and fails the build if it does. (2) The district overlay had a second, unrelated cause that would have survived the worker fix. Attachment waited on map.once(idle), and idle requires style.loaded(), which requires every source to report loaded - but the MapTiler styles declare a maptiler_attribution source that is a vector source carrying only an attribution string, with no url, no tiles, and no layer referencing it. It has nothing to fetch, so its loaded flag is false forever, map.loaded() is never true, and idle never fires. Attachment now waits on getStyle().layers, the public signal that the stylesheet is parsed, which is the only precondition addSource and addLayer actually have. Evidence, measured in-page: 6 basemap tiles fetched from the .pbf template and all 6 parsed into buckets, 557 rendered basemap features across 13 layers including Water, so the land/water edge test passes; districts draw with 6 geojson-vt tiles, 11 rendered features, labels AZ-7 and AZ-6, ocdId ocd-division/country:us/state:az/cd:7. Note that .pbf fetches originate inside the worker and are invisible to main-thread resource timing, which is why the earlier pbf=0 evidence could not distinguish a dead worker from a throttled render loop; tile bucket state is the reliable signal. Raster branch, rasterBasemapEnabled, the NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_RASTER flag and the OpenFreeMap fallback are all deleted; resolveBasemap now returns null without a key and the caller shows Basemap unavailable. The error filter in map-canvas.tsx now logs every MapLibre error and filters only which ones raise a user-facing notice. Branch claude/civic-map-entry-screen-4ey1cs; test (26 pass), lint and build all pass.

Item: Design system port from EdiaStratMap
Detail: Replace the public-notice palette with EdiaStratMap tokens, swap typography to DM Sans plus JetBrains Mono, and add a persisted light/dark theme toggle.
Notes: 2026-08-11. Ported :root and [data-theme=light] token sets from EdiaStratMap src/styles/main.css. Edia drives its UI from three accents (strat/cust/both); ours are the three government tiers, so --accent-local, --accent-state, --accent-national and --accent-all each with a -glow variant, plus --concluded, --canceled and --district-line. Typography is DM Sans for all UI text and JetBrains Mono for every numeral, identifier, OCD-ID, date and time, both loaded as variable fonts through next/font/google. Theme toggle persists under wtp.theme using the same useSyncExternalStore shape as use-stored-zip (frozen pending snapshot, cached against the raw stored string) and writes data-theme on <html>; an inline pre-paint script in app/layout.tsx applies it before first paint, because no hook runs early enough to prevent a flash. Legacy ink/paper/signal Tailwind aliases are kept in an explicitly marked block so the existing entry screen keeps rendering; they are to be deleted as Phase 2/3 replaces those components. Two things went beyond the brief and are worth knowing. (1) The basemap now follows the theme (basic-v2-dark / basic-v2, both overridable by env). EdiaStratMap does not theme its map, but it does not need to - it draws dark panels over a single light OSM layer, whereas ours is a dark vector style, so a fixed basemap would have put light panels over a dark map. (2) lib/map/districts.ts no longer hardcodes its colours; it reads --district-line and --bg off the document when it builds the layers, so globals.css is the single source of truth. Two real bugs were found and fixed doing this, both in the silent-failure family. A restyle effect written with a skip-the-first-run flag fired a spurious setStyle while the initial style was still loading and wedged the renderer, because React Strict Mode re-invokes effects against the same component instance and the flag reads as already spent on the second pass; it is now keyed on the style URL actually applied, which is idempotent under any number of runs. And re-attaching the district overlay after setStyle with once(styledata) silently lost it, because styledata fires for the outgoing style before the new one is applied, so the guard saw the layers still present, skipped the re-add, and the incoming style then wiped them - light mode came up with no districts and nothing logged. District attachment is now a standing invariant subscribed to every styledata and guarded on wanted-absent-and-parsed, so it self-heals after any style change. Verified with pnpm shoot in both themes: 655 rendered basemap features across 13 layers, 26 district features, 12 markers, correct token values and data-theme in each. Branch claude/civic-map-entry-screen-4ey1cs; test (26 pass), lint, tsc and build all pass.

Item: Screenshot tooling
Detail: Headless Playwright capture of the running app, so visual checks do not depend on a browser window being visible.
Notes: 2026-08-11. scripts/shoot.mts plus pnpm shoot <name> [--zip] [--theme] [--districts] [--viewport] [--path]. Added because MapLibre renders on requestAnimationFrame, which browsers stop delivering to an occluded or backgrounded tab: both the in-app browser pane and an attached Chrome reported visibilityState hidden whenever the editor window covered them, so captures came back stale or empty and timer-based checks hit CDP timeouts (background tabs clamp setInterval to one second). A headless Chromium is never occluded, so shots are reproducible regardless of what is on screen. The script seeds localStorage before first paint rather than clicking through the UI, forces reducedMotion so the camera lands deterministically, and prints what actually rendered - style layer count, rendered feature count, district layer and feature counts, marker count, resolved theme - so a screenshot can never quietly be of an empty map. It reaches the map instance by walking the React fiber, since the map is deliberately not exposed on window. Output goes to screenshots/, which is gitignored. Playwright is a devDependency; approved by the author before adding.

Item: Counsel question: vendor terms vs. public records duty
Detail: Can a software vendor's terms narrow statutory access to records a public body must publish?
Notes: For B05. Framing: agendas are made and used by a district in the course of official duty, and open meeting law obliges the district to post them in advance. A public record does not stop being a public record because a vendor holds it, and a vendor's website terms are not a mechanism by which a public body can narrow statutory access to its own records. Live constraint on the whole local wedge, not a formality - the answer determines whether the school-board tier is reachable at all, so it is worth asking early. Item: handoff --ship leaves local main stale
Detail: --ship merges the PR on GitHub but never fast-forwards local main, so local main sits a whole session behind. Checking it out makes the repo look empty.
Notes: Found 2026-08-12 at session start. The working tree was on main at 64fee33 - the initial "Add files via upload" commit carrying only CLAUDE.md - while origin/main was at 2978324 with 26 commits and 118 files. Every phase of work was present and safe on origin; local main had simply never been updated, because scripts/handoff.mjs merges the PR through gh and then leaves the session on the feature branch. Nothing in the repo pulls main afterwards, so it goes stale by one session every time and the next checkout of main presents an apparently empty project. Recovered with git merge --ff-only origin/main: local main held zero unique commits and was a strict ancestor, and none of the untracked files (public/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs, screenshots/, next-env.d.ts, tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, .env.local) collided with a tracked path, so the fast-forward was lossless. 68/68 tests pass on the restored tree. Fix: have --ship fast-forward local main after a successful merge, and have the plain handoff check report main being behind origin/main as a warning - it currently only checks the branch against its own upstream and main against the branch, never local main against origin/main, which is the exact gap that hid this. SECOND GAP IN THE SAME SCRIPT, hit 2026-08-12: --ship refuses outright on a branch that has no upstream yet (ship() returns early on "refused - no upstream to push to"). It assumes the branch was already pushed by hand at some point, which is true for a long-lived branch and false for every new one - so the first --ship of every session fails until someone runs git push -u by hand. It should push -u origin HEAD itself when there is no upstream, which is the same one-line class of fix as fast-forwarding main afterwards. Both ends of the script assume a branch that already exists on the remote. FIXED 2026-08-12, branch claude/fix-r07-fast-forward-main. DONE: test (79 pass), lint and build all green. All three parts of this row are closed. (1) --ship fast-forwards local main after a successful merge, via git fetch origin main:main - it moves the ref WITHOUT touching the working tree and refuses anything that is not a fast-forward, so a diverged main is reported, never flattened. Git rejects that fetch form when main is the checked-out branch, so from main it is git merge --ff-only origin/main instead. It runs after the post-ship re-measure and before git-state.txt is rewritten, so the report and the mirror file both describe the state the session actually ends in. (2) --ship pushes -u origin HEAD when the branch has no upstream instead of refusing; a branch created this session having no upstream is the normal case, and refusing meant the first ship of every session failed until someone ran git push -u by hand. (3) The plain handoff check now reports local main against origin/main as its own checklist line, which is the comparison nothing else made - branch vs its own upstream and main vs the branch both read clean while local main sat a session behind. SAFETY: fastForwardMain refuses when local main is AHEAD of origin/main and says so rather than doing anything, and git rejects the non-fast-forward underneath as a second line of defence. Verified both: with a commit only on local main the check reported "diverged - 0 behind, 1 ahead of origin/main" and a manual git fetch origin main:main was rejected non-fast-forward with the local ref unmoved. Verified in a sandbox with a bare local origin rather than reasoned about: a branch with no upstream got one from --ship ("feature pushed, now tracking origin/feature"); after advancing origin main to simulate the merge, the plain check warned "2 commit(s) behind origin/main - git fetch origin main:main"; that fetch fast-forwarded the ref with git status --porcelain empty afterwards, proving the working tree is untouched. The gh-dependent PR steps cannot run against a local remote, so the full --ship path was exercised for real when this row shipped. The suggested command adapts to where you are standing - git fetch origin main:main from a branch, git merge --ff-only origin/main from main - because the fetch form is rejected for the checked-out branch and printing a command that cannot work is worse than printing none.

Item: Mirror comparison is raw-byte, so a line-ending mismatch forces a full recopy
Detail: sameBytes() does not normalize CRLF. Dormant now that both sides are CRLF, but nothing stops it recurring.
Notes: Filed 2026-08-12 and CORRECTED the same session, because the first version overstated it. What was claimed: that the mirror line can never report identical on Windows and recopies all five files every session. That is wrong - after one sync the handoff check reported "mirror 5 already current", and both sides now measure identical (CLAUDE.md 140 CRLF / 140 LF on each side, state.md 1337, tracker.csv 88). What actually happened: the mirror held LF copies from an earlier era while the git checkout produces CRLF, so the first comparison flagged all four as differing, one sync rewrote them as CRLF, and they have matched since. A one-time mismatch that has already self-healed, not a permanent failure. Keeping this open at P3 because the underlying fragility is real: scripts/handoff.mjs line 186 calls sameBytes(from, to) on raw bytes while the divergence check just below it at line 207 does normalize CRLF, so the two halves of the same function disagree about what "same" means. Any future write of the mirror with LF - a different tool, a non-Windows checkout, a hand edit in an editor that normalizes - silently reintroduces a full recopy and a red line on the one gate meant to catch a genuinely diverged mirror. Fix: normalize line endings in sameBytes, or add a .gitattributes pinning the four mirrored docs to LF so the working tree and the mirror agree by construction. The second also stops CRLF churn showing up in diffs. Lesson worth keeping separately: this row was written from one --check run without testing what a sync did, which is the same measure-first failure as the 4.5.1 write-up. || 2026-08-17 (g7) HARDENED BOTH WAYS, on the author's ruling "harden now" - the row named two fixes and both shipped, because they close different halves. THE SYMPTOM: sameBytes() is renamed sameContent() and normalizes CRLF for text entries, since raw bytes were the bug. The two halves of the mirror step disagreed about what "same" means - the comparison read raw bytes while the divergence check twenty lines below already normalized. Binary entries KEEP the raw comparison, for the reason the divergence check already records: newline-normalizing an .xlsx compares two corrupted strings. That flag is now computed BEFORE the comparison and passed into it; computing it afterwards is precisely what let the two halves drift apart. The text path also drops the size shortcut, which was itself the bug in miniature - two files differing only in line endings have different sizes and identical content. THE CAUSE: .gitattributes now pins the ten text mirrored docs to eol=lf and marks deferred.xlsx binary, so the working tree and the mirror agree by construction rather than by both remembering to normalize. The ten are the text half of MIRRORED_DOCS; that module stays authoritative for WHAT is mirrored. The working tree was normalized in the same commit so the pin takes effect now rather than at the next checkout: 9 files rewritten CRLF to LF (deferred.md was already LF), and git diff --stat confirms ZERO content change - the LF form matched what git already stored, byte for byte. NOT DORMANT AFTER ALL, and this is the correction to the row's own earlier assessment. Measured live this session: CLAUDE.md is 45417 bytes in the working tree and 45147 in git, a 270-byte gap that is exactly its 270 CRLF line endings. PROVED ON THE REAL DRIVE MIRROR rather than a fixture, using the natural experiment this session created - the mirror still holds CRLF copies while the working tree is now LF. Old logic reports 2 of 11 current; new logic reports 10 of 11. EIGHT FILES would have been needlessly recopied on every run, every run, forever: CLAUDE.md, abuse-policy.md, vendor-review.md, source-ladder.md, defects.md, state.md, types.ts, deferred.csv. The eleventh, tracker.csv, correctly still differs - this session edited it. That is the failure the row predicted, observed: a permanently red line on the one gate meant to catch a genuinely diverged mirror. Branch claude/g7-dispositions-0817; test 793 pass 0 fail, lint 0 errors, tsc --noEmit clean, build green.

Item: session:start, and a dev server that can be stopped
Detail: Three start-of-session checks and a pid-tracked dev server, so a stale main, a clobbered CLAUDE.md or last session server cannot pass for a working one.
Notes: 2026-08-12, branch claude/session-start-and-dev-server. DONE: test (79 pass), lint and build all green. THREE PIECES, one shared property - the environment lies quietly if you do not look. A stale main looks like an empty repo, a clobbered CLAUDE.md looks like a repo with no constraints, a stale dev server looks like a working build. None announces itself; each presents as a plausible working state that is the wrong one. Recorded as a table in docs/state.md section 8. 1. scripts/session-start.mjs (pnpm session:start): fetch and compare local main to origin/main, printing the commit count and the git merge --ff-only command on a miss (R07); check CLAUDE.md is roughly 10 KB, failing under 1 KB or on the bare @AGENTS.md line with a restore-from-mirror command and NEVER a suggestion to reconstruct it; check port 3000 is free; then start the dev server through pnpm dev so predev runs. Exits non-zero on any failure. --check runs the three checks and starts nothing, which is the form a hook wants since the plain form ends in a server that never exits. A DIVERGED main (commits both sides) is reported separately and gets no --ff-only suggestion, because it would refuse. 2. Dev-server lifecycle. pnpm dev is now scripts/dev.mjs, which spawns next dev and writes its pid to .dev-server.pid (gitignored), removed on any exit it lives to see. predev is check-port.mjs then build-map-worker.mjs: it refuses when 3000 is in use rather than letting Next slide to 3001, naming the occupying pid, whether it is this repo own server, and the kill command. Sliding to 3001 is the failure worth preventing - scripts/shoot.mts targets a fixed localhost:3000, so screenshots would be of the old build AND the old map worker, since predev is where that bundle regenerates. 3. pnpm handoff stops the dev server before syncing the mirror, as its own checklist line. Non-fatal when nothing is running. It will NOT kill on a guess: something on 3000 with no matching pid file is reported foreign, with pid and kill command, for a person to decide. If the port is still held after the kill it FAILS and exits non-zero - a handoff reporting the session closed while something still serves is a false report. TWO THINGS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The pid holding the socket is NOT the pid in the file: Next runs the server in start-server.js, a grandchild of next dev. Measured - file recorded 5544, port held by 5816, and the stale server found at session start was four processes deep (17608 cmd shim -> 27420 next dev -> 23496 start-server -> 25956). So kills take the tree and the file-matches-occupant test is descent, not ===; an identity test would call this repo own server a stranger and withhold the kill that works. Second, dev.mjs resolves next/dist/bin/next and runs it under node rather than through the .cmd shim, because the old "dev": "next dev" put cmd.exe /d /s /c between pnpm and Next and killing a shim on Windows can orphan what it launched. FOUND A REAL ONE ON THE FIRST RUN: session:start --check failed on port 3000 held by pid 23496, a next dev started 16:06 that had survived the previous session handoff - exactly the gap this closes. It reported foreign rather than killing it, because it predated the pid file. All paths exercised rather than reasoned about: clean pass; the real stale server; predev refusal both directly and through pnpm (confirming the && chain works in a pnpm script on Windows and that Next never starts); pid file written on dev and removed when Next was killed underneath the wrapper; handoff --check reporting without killing; handoff killing the tree and confirming the port free; foreign holder warning; and the still-occupied path forced with a decoy pid plus an independent holder, which failed and exited 1. Does NOT close R07. session:start reports stale main and prints the fix; --ship still does not fast-forward, and the handoff checklist still does not warn. 2026-08-13, branch claude/deploy-snapshot-and-demo: the missing half added — session:start now KILLS a stale dev server it can attribute to this repo (pid file match) instead of failing, still fails on a foreign occupant, and after starting waits for / to serve then verifies the port holder descends from the child it spawned, printing the HEAD sha served. Verified live: killed-and-started clean, confirmation line printed.

Item: Tucson agenda source - not Legistar, and the vendor terms forbid the portal

Notes: Found 2026-08-12 while doing D12, by following the clerk page rather than guessing slugs - the 4.6.7 CMS rule doing its job. tucson, tucsonaz and cityoftucson ALL return 500 from the Legistar API: Tucson is not a Granicus Legistar client. tucsonaz.gov runs on Granicus OpenCities, which is the WEBSITE CMS - inferring the agenda vendor from it would have concluded "Granicus, therefore Legistar" and been wrong twice. Item: New Hampshire wording - a missing agenda there can be lawful, not our gap
Detail: NH does not require an agenda at all, so NO_SOURCE_FOUND must not read as our coverage failure.
Notes: Found 2026-08-12 doing the D14 statute review. NH RSA 91-A:2 requires notice of time, date and place posted in two public places or a newspaper 24h ahead, and the municipality website may be one of them - but it DOES NOT REQUIRE AN AGENDA, and a body may take up topics not on one it chose to publish. Compare AZ A.R.S. 38-431.02, which requires the agenda posted on the body website, and NJ N.J.S.A. 10:4-8, which requires it only "to the extent known". The 4.6.6 coverage language currently says we do not have a body calendar YET, which reads as our gap. For a New Hampshire body that can be the body lawful choice and there may be nothing to find. Affects 03255 Newbury and every NH body in the registry. Decide the wording before implementing - misattributing a legal choice to our own coverage is the same family of error as claiming unincorporated without measuring it. 2026-08-12 WORDING DECIDED BY THE AUTHOR AND IMPLEMENTED, branch claude/link-ladder-and-coverage-audit (this row first named branch claude/d17-nh-agenda-wording, which NEVER EXISTED - all of 4.6.10, 4.6.9 and the D17 wording landed on the one branch above; recorded rather than tidied over, same as the D03 slip). Item: Overlapping pins swallow each other clicks
Detail: Two venues within a few metres on screen render overlapping markers; the top one intercepts clicks meant for the other.
Notes: 2026-08-17 (g9, branch claude/g9-r39-r40-queue-0817). THE AUTHOR RULED A, SPIDERFY (2026-08-17) and that is what was built - nothing clusters, nothing merges, nothing is hidden. WHY THE OTHER TWO OPTIONS IN THIS ROW WERE NOT TAKEN, recorded so nobody re-proposes them: clustering replaces pins with a number, which costs the reader a click the map never used to need, and reader friction is a defect with the standing of a wrong number; raising the grouping precision by zoom would MERGE two different governments' venues into one pin, and a merged pin is a claim that two buildings are one place. THE BUILD: lib/map/spiderfy.ts holds the geometry as pure functions - findCollisionGroups (union-find over projected screen points, TRANSITIVE so an A-B-C chain is one group and not two overlapping pairs, stable ordering so the same collision fans the same way every time, singletons are never groups) and fanOffsets (a ring for up to eight, an Archimedean spiral beyond, with the ring radius solved from the chord so adjacent pins always clear the collision radius). lib/map/marker-pool.ts gains applySpiderfy/clearSpiderfy, moving markers by MapLibre's own setOffset in screen pixels - NOT a CSS transform, because MapLibre owns the element's transform and rewrites it every frame, so a fanned group survives a pan and a zoom. components/map/map-canvas.tsx puts the fan IN FRONT of selection: a press on a stacked pin fans the group and selects nothing (a click landing on a stack is a click whose target the reader has not chosen), the next press selects normally, and a pin that never collides still opens in ONE press. DISMISSAL: a press on the map itself (the canvas click, which markers never reach because they are DOM overlays) and Escape beside it, per M90's reason that a gesture nobody discovers is not an exit. No history entry (M52). A fanned pin renders a dashed halo so a pin sitting away from its building is not read as a wrong location, and deliberately NOT in colour - pin colour already means which level of government meets there. TESTS: tests/spiderfy.test.ts, 10 of 10, including the load-bearing one - at EVERY group size from 2 to 14, re-running the collision detector over the FANNED positions returns zero groups, so "every member is individually reachable" is asserted rather than eyeballed. WALK: two checks appended to scripts/walk-all.mts section M, run at DESKTOP width. Verified live at 85701: 4 pins in one Tucson stack, 4 fanned, every pair clearing 28px, and Escape returning all four to within 2px. TWO DIAGNOSED WALK DEFECTS FIXED IN THE SAME PASS, both found by the check's own first run: it ran at 390 where the who-governs card covers the middle of the map, so the press landed on an overlay and reported a working fan as broken - it now runs wide AND asserts via elementFromPoint that the press CAN land, reporting a covered point as CANNOT-RUN rather than FAIL; and the dismissal check passed trivially beside its failing sibling (0 fanned, nothing moved, all true and all meaningless), so it is now gated on the fan having actually opened. Screenshots screenshots/m19-before.png and m19-fanned.png. EVIDENCE: test 865 pass 0 fail (10 new) / lint 0 errors, 16 warnings all pre-existing / build exit 0.

Item: Marker pool - reuse markers instead of rebuilding them
Detail: Markers created once and reused across filter changes, with visibility diffed rather than the set rebuilt.
Notes: 2026-08-12, branch claude/phase-6-popup-and-modal. Evidence: test (132 pass), lint and build green; verified on screen at 85701 and 85641 (12 markers rendered, selection and filtering intact). lib/map/marker-pool.ts ports buildMarkerPool/rebuildMarkerPool/updateMarkerIcon and the _previouslyVisiblePoolKeys diffing. THE POINT IS THE SPLIT: rebuildMarkerPool runs when the DATA changes and creates/removes; applyVisibility runs when a FILTER changes and touches only the pins whose visibility actually flipped, so narrowing 500 pins to 480 does 20 DOM writes rather than 980. A filtered-out pin is HIDDEN (data-hidden, display:none), never destroyed. updateMarkerIcon mutates an existing element rather than replacing it, because replacing drops focus and these are real buttons somebody may be tabbing through. The click handler reads entry.venue at click time rather than closing over the venue, so a pin updated in place cannot hand back a stale one. applyVisibility RETURNS the number of elements it wrote to - if that ever approaches the pool size on an ordinary filter change, the diffing has stopped working. Built now deliberately: at 34 fixtures this is invisible, and once real ingestion lands there is nothing small enough left to verify a rewrite against.

Item: Verify a branch exists before naming it
Detail: A commit message or tracker Note that names a branch must name a branch that exists. git branch --list <name> before writing it, in the handoff flow or as a habit; two sessions have now named branches that were never created.
Notes: Opened 2026-08-13. Last session commit messages and tracker Notes named claude/meeting-bodies-join and claude/d17-nh-agenda-wording; neither ever existed — all commits were on one branch, caught and corrected after the fact (state.md 7). R03 requires a branch name plus checks passed, but nothing verifies the branch is real. A DELETED BRANCH STILL COUNTS AS REAL, which is the whole design problem: branches are merged and deleted as the normal end of their life, so git branch --list alone would report every correctly-closed branch as a fabrication and the check would cry wolf far more often than not - the same argument R19 makes about noise. So a name is real if ANY of three routes remembers it: a local or remote ref, a merge-commit subject (Merge pull request #N from <owner>/<branch>), or the reflog. A name none of them remembers is reported as UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE rather than as proof of bad faith - a branch pushed from another machine and squash-merged could in principle leave no trace - but the row still needs fixing either way, because a Note nobody can verify is not evidence. Reports, never blocks: the rows it flags are history, and failing a ship over old prose would teach everyone to skip the line. STEP 1, WHAT OPENCIVICDATA ACTUALLY DOES, read 2026-08-17 from identifiers/country-us.csv (194,977 identifiers): THERE IS A CONVENTION AND IT IS CONSISTENT. A special district gets a segment named for its FUNCTION, nested under the county that contains it (or the state where it spans counties), slugged from its own published name — state:ca/county:los_angeles/water:castaic_lake_water_agency, state:nc/county:carteret/sanitation:harkers_island, state:mn/county:hennepin/park_district:1, state:il/sewer:mwrd. Six such segment types exist nationally — water, sanitation, sewer, park_district, health_care, transit — across FIFTY-ONE identifiers in the whole country. There is no community_college segment anywhere in the file; the phrase appears only twice, as school_district: slugs for two Maricopa DBAs. STEP 2, AND IT DECIDES THE ANSWER: the list carries NONE of the governments this repo needs. Arizona's segment types in full are country, state, cd, county, council_district, precinct, school_district, court_of_appeals, place, ward, sldl, sldu. BUILT, three answers, a test per type. lib/corpus/positions.ts answers what has this person said about X in exactly one of three ways, and the reason there are three is the one types.ts recorded when it refused to render from this corpus at all: an empty match reads as this person has no position on X, which is a false claim about a named person. MATCHED renders verbatim passages, each with the page it came from and the date we read it. SEARCHED_NOTHING_MATCHED renders OUR search WITH ITS DENOMINATOR - we read N pages and none mentioned it - and says in as many words that it is not a statement that they have no position. NOT_YET_COLLECTED is a DIFFERENT SENTENCE about a different thing, our collection rather than our search, and it offers their own page. Unreadable snapshots are counted separately and never as searched: a page we could not read is a page we did not search, and counting it would inflate the number that makes the answer honest. The three mark themselves in the DOM, only MATCHED renders a quote block, and a test asserts a named gap never wears a present value's styling. CHANGE MARKERS: a second snapshot of a URL with a different hash renders this page changed since <date> - dates only, never what changed and never what it means; a guard asserts the module cannot emit flip-flopped, reversed, softened, contradicts or inconsistent. SURFACE: the Positions section in the large popup, topic-searchable against this person's corpus only (the subject is in the route's PATH, so it cannot answer for anyone else - the D40 distinctness rule), with a CURATED topic chip list rather than one derived from the corpus, because a topic list read off what a candidate chose to talk about is a characterisation by omission. THE BROWSER RUNG IS BUILT AND THE OBVIOUS GUESS WAS WRONG: a Chrome User-Agent is not the rung. Node's fetch sending a full browser header set is still 403'd by both hosts; curl sending the IDENTICAL headers is served 200 — the filter reads the TLS/HTTP2 client fingerprint, so a session that swapped the UA, got another 403 and recorded a closed route would have been wrong. politeGetText(url, {profile:'browser'}) sends the browser header set in-process and re-issues through curl on a 403, keeping 'we-the-people civic meeting index (contact: …)' at the end of the User-Agent both ways: a browser to a filter, ourselves to a human. No login, no token, no robots directive names these paths. WHAT WAS BEHIND THE WALL: Kearsarge publishes its whole 2026-2027 calendar as a two-column month table (39 sittings, the board's own words beside many — 'Staff Nominations', 'Budget Presentations', 'Warrant Discussion'), 'Meetings start at 6:30 PM' and 'Meeting Location: 114 Main Street, New London'; the 2026-08-13 audit had 165 Main St from a search snippet and the page says 114. Item: The Census geocoder cannot be called from a browser at all - D53's device-side promise needs a transport the author rules on
Detail: PROVEN IN A REAL CHROMIUM, not inferred: geocoding.geo.census.gov answers 200 to a server and sends NO Access-Control-Allow-Origin header (it sends Vary: Origin and nothing else), so every browser fetch fails with TypeError: Failed to fetch. Notes: Done 2026-08-15, the author's ruling. app/api/geocode is a stateless POST proxy: no log row, no store, no header echoed, nothing printed, no cache, response no-store. Guarded BOTH ways in tests/geocoder.test.ts - a source scan for every write primitive AND a runtime call proving nothing was written and only {match,lat,lng} comes back. The reader-facing promise changed in the SAME commit on both surfaces, from the unkeepable 'never sent to us' to 'your address passes through our server to the Census Bureau's geocoder; we never store or log it'; the coupling is guard-tested and the old sentence is asserted GONE. Item: The deploy gate - pnpm handoff --ship runs the build Netlify runs, and refuses on failure
Detail: Born from main@705f73b: merged green, Netlify failed type-check on a walk SCRIPT, production served the previous build for an hour.
Notes: 2026-08-16 (branch claude/deploy-gate-0816). THE FAILURE: Netlify's build for 705f73b failed on scripts/walk-0815g.mts(313,23) TS18048 - 'found.zba' is possibly 'undefined'. Site code compiled clean; a walk script stopped the truck. THE TYPE ERROR: an undiscriminated union ({error:number} | {total,zba,first}) narrowed with `"zba" in found`, which narrows nothing because TS widens such a union so BOTH members carry every key with one optional-undefined. Fixed with a real `ok` discriminant, no ! assertion; an unreachable service now THROWS a named error while a zero count stays a loud failed check - a check(...,false) there would have read as 'the Zoning Board is missing from production', a different and far more alarming claim. DIAGNOSIS BEFORE THE FIX, both suspects tested: stale .next skipping the type-check is WRONG (a warm-cache pnpm build on the same tree reproduces the failure exactly - compiled in 718ms, then 'Running TypeScript ...', then the identical TS18048); the build ran BEFORE the file existed is RIGHT and is the whole answer - the last pnpm build was in the pre-documents checks, the walk script was written after, and between writing it and shipping only pnpm walk:0815g ran. An ORDERING gap, not a cache bug, which is what decided the gate's home. THE GATE: buildGate() in scripts/handoff.mjs runs `pnpm run build` - the exact command netlify.toml gives Netlify - with tsconfig.tsbuildinfo cleared first, before the first push, and refuses the ship on failure with the TS diagnostic printed (Netlify's log needs the author's login, so a gate that only said 'build failed' would move the wall rather than remove it). NOT tsc --noEmit: tsconfig includes .next/types/**/*.ts, the route types Next GENERATES during a build, so a bare tsc checks whatever they said last time and a bad route-handler signature is exactly what it could miss. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, recorded: a .githooks/pre-push hook - it would catch a push that bypasses handoff, but it is installed by `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` which is per-clone and which session:start only REPORTS on, so it can be silently absent in a fresh clone; and it would fire on every WIP push, which is how a minute-long check gets --no-verify'd away. NO SKIP FLAG, deliberately. PROVEN by injecting a deliberate TS error into the same walk script and running the gate's body against it: refused with 'scripts/walk-0815g.mts(352,5): error TS2532 · Failed to type check.'; tree restored, tsc exits 0. tests/handoff-gate.test.ts guards the WIRING (called before the first push, result acted on, same command as netlify.toml, tsbuildinfo cleared, no skip flag) - a source scan on purpose, since running a production build inside pnpm test would take the suite from 3s to 2min and would be testing Next. Evidence: test 606 pass (2 new) / lint clean (8 pre-existing warnings) / build exit 0; gate green in 9s on the shipping run; PR #44 merged, main 6a6dbbd, production serving it ~4 minutes later. || 2026-08-17 (g7) THE GATE GAINS ITS SECOND HALF - a deploy is now verified to have LANDED, not merely to have built. On the author's earlier ruling: an endpoint returning the commit SHA the deploy was built from, so a deploy with no visible output is verifiable. THE GAP THIS CLOSES, stated precisely because the two claims are easy to conflate: R22 proves the TREE BUILDS by running the same command Netlify runs, before shipping. It cannot prove that what Netlify then SERVED is this commit. The hour of production serving a previous build is exactly the distance between them. NEW: app/api/build/route.ts. Returns commit, commitShort, branch, context and deployId from Netlify's COMMIT_REF/BRANCH/CONTEXT/DEPLOY_ID. Read at MODULE SCOPE with the full process.env.X property access written out literally - Next only inlines a build-time env reference it can statically see, and a dynamic read (process.env[name]) would return undefined at runtime, which is the quiet way this endpoint would report nothing forever. Absent variables render "unknown" rather than a plausible SHA: absence is never dressed as a value, and an endpoint that invents its own answer is worse than no endpoint. Served no-store, because a cached build stamp is precisely the lie it exists to prevent. Nothing enumerates process.env - only named, non-secret build metadata - since that is how a token reaches a public JSON body. WIRED: handoff --ship now calls verifyDeployLanded() after the merge and fast-forward succeed (and only then, or the SHA polled for would be the wrong one). It polls /api/build for up to 5 minutes against origin/main's sha and declares itself with the C05 synthetic-run header. A TIMEOUT REPORTS AS COULD-NOT-RUN, NEVER AS A FAILURE - Netlify's build queue is not this script's to wait on, and an unreachable service is not a missing feature, the same distinction walk:all draws. What it will not do is report success without having seen the SHA. IT ALSO CARRIES EVIDENCE FOR THE WRITE GUARD'S SECOND REMAINDER (R34): the response's buildEnv block reports what the BUILD saw and the runtime block reports what the SERVING PROCESS sees - NETLIFY, CONTEXT, DEPLOY_ID presence, NODE_ENV, and the dbRole the guard would conclude. A variable present in buildEnv and absent in runtime is a build-only variable the write guard must not depend on. That is a fact nobody could check without deploying and looking, which is why the guard was built on NODE_ENV and the tightening was deferred rather than guessed. VERIFIED LOCALLY against a real dev server: the route answers {"commit":"unknown", ..., "runtime":{"nodeEnv":"development","hasNetlify":false,"dbRole":"production"}} - honest on all counts, since a local build has no COMMIT_REF and WTP_DB_ROLE is unset. The Netlify-side values are readable on the first --ship after this lands. Branch claude/g7-dispositions-0817; test 793 pass 0 fail, tsc --noEmit clean, build green. || CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (g8), branch claude/g8-deploy-and-g7-queue-0817. THE BUILD-STAMP ENDPOINT SHIPPED WITH A FALSE PREMISE AND COULD NEVER HAVE VERIFIED A DEPLOY. Found by using it: after PR #72 merged, handoff polled /api/build for five minutes and production kept answering {""commit"":""unknown"",""buildEnv"":{""hasCommitRef"":false,...}} with HTTP 200. THE PREMISE, quoted from the row above: 'Next inlines a build-time env reference it can statically see' into the server bundle. IT DOES NOT. Next inlines for the CLIENT; server code keeps process.env.X as a RUNTIME read. Measured rather than reasoned about - the built chunk .next/server/chunks/_1nq4lm3._.js still contained the literal text 'process.env.COMMIT_REF??null'. Netlify sets COMMIT_REF in the BUILD environment and not in the function runtime, so the module-scope read ran at cold start, found undefined, and the endpoint reported 'unknown' on every request of every deploy. The failure the row's own header warned about, arriving through the other door: not a dynamic lookup defeating the inlining, but no inlining ever happening. THE FIX: next.config.ts's env key, which is the mechanism that actually substitutes at build time, exposing WTP_BUILD_COMMIT / _BRANCH / _CONTEXT / _DEPLOY_ID / _ON_NETLIFY; the route reads those. Build metadata only - anything inlined there is readable by anyone who can read the bundle. An absent variable is written as an empty string by the config and read as NULL by the route, because '' sliced to seven characters is a blank SHA rendered as a value, which is the render-default rule in the one place whose job is being trustworthy about which commit is serving. PROVEN EMPIRICALLY, twice over: COMMIT_REF=deadbeefcafe1234 pnpm build puts the literal into the server chunk AND removes process.env.WTP_BUILD_COMMIT from it (so it was substituted, not merely present), and next start then answers {""commit"":""deadbeefcafe1234"",""commitShort"":""deadbee""}. GUARDED: tests/build-stamp.test.ts, 5 tests, asserting the two files agree name-for-name - the rot this cannot afford is a name added to one and not the other, which reads as an absent variable and renders the same wrong 'unknown' while looking correct. The runtime block's direct reads of NETLIFY, CONTEXT and DEPLOY_ID are deliberately EXEMPT and separately asserted to still exist: they are the measurement R34's second remainder needs, not the defect. AND THAT MEASUREMENT NOW HAS AN ANSWER, which is a finding in its own right: on the live Netlify deploy the serving function sees NEITHER NETLIFY nor CONTEXT nor DEPLOY_ID (hasNetlify false, hasContext false, hasDeployId false, contextValue null) while the response headers say Server: Netlify with an X-Nf-Request-Id. So there is NO runtime signal from Netlify for the write guard to tighten on, and the guard must keep resting on NODE_ENV plus the belt. Recorded so the next session does not go looking for one.

Item: The active-state model, built as specified - and the mask stops muting the state the reader is standing in
Detail: The author's g5 item 1. One state active at a time; the WHOLE of it crisp at every zoom; every other state muted and lowered; no state active means no treatment at all. Zip shading removed from the product.
Notes: 2026-08-16 (g5), branch claude/active-state-model-0816. DIAGNOSED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY READING: at the zoom a reader lands on from a zip (z11) the ENTIRE frame was muted and blurred - no crisp pixel anywhere - while the reader stood in the middle of the active state. The mute is a DOM scrim carrying backdrop-filter, clipped to everything-except-the-active-state by clip-path: url(#...). The path fed to that clip was the state's rings projected at FULL EXTENT: measured on production, Arizona at z11 spans x -10869.4..5939.9 and y -16547.3..3432.1, about 16,800 x 20,000 CSS px. CHROMIUM SILENTLY DROPS A CLIP PATH THAT LARGE, and a dropped clip is not a smaller clip - the scrim then paints over its whole box. Proved by holding the TOPOLOGY fixed (viewport rectangle minus one enclosing rectangle, even-odd, an empty region at every size) and varying only the magnitude: +/-2000px gave chroma 17.39 detail 20.15, pixel-identical to the effect-disabled frame; +/-8000px and +/-20000px both gave chroma 11.24 detail 9.57, pixel-identical to the broken frame. Also found: the CSS `mask` on the scrim was INERT the whole time - Chromium does not resolve an SVG <mask> reference from CSS on an HTML element - so the clip was the only thing doing the work and its failure took the entire effect with it. Same class as g4's clamped SVG filter region: Chromium's answer to geometry it cannot rasterize is to drop it, and a dropped mask reads as FULL coverage, the loudest way an ambient effect can fail. FIX: lib/map/state-focus.ts#clipRingToBox - Sutherland-Hodgman per ring against the mask's own region (canvas + FILTER_PAD), applied after projection and BEFORE simplification. Nothing outside that box was ever visible, so the cut removes only geometry that was being rasterized to be thrown away, and it is also the cheapest frame win available. The case that looks identical in the code and opposite on screen is handled explicitly: a ring clipped to NOTHING means the viewport does not touch the active state, so the whole frame is muted (pan into New Mexico with Arizona active) - it used to clear the drawing and render plain, which is the no-active-state treatment. Holes survive the clip, so a viewport inside a hole cancels to nothing under even-odd, which is the truth. ZIP SHADING REMOVED WHOLE per the author's ruling: the tint, both layers, the source, the /api/zcta/<zip> route, lib/geo/zcta-outline.ts and the client fetch are deleted - not flagged off. NEW PERMANENT MEASUREMENT pnpm measure:focus (scripts/measure-focus.mts): the existing pnpm measure:extrusion passed at full marks on this broken build because it measures how SMOOTHLY the edge falls off, not WHAT is covered. The new one is anchored to lng/lat - real places projected through the live map - and asserts interior crispness far from the entered zip (north Tucson, Drexel Heights, the corners of the state), effect-off equivalence with the border excluded by the SHIPPED spec's own reach rather than by a constant, exterior muting compared point-against-itself, per-state data scoping off the network log, and no-active-state at 06716 and with no zip. Item: The meetings panel renders empty until the mouse moves - a paint failure, not a data one

THE AUTHOR'S OBJECTION WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE SCRIM AND WRONG ABOUT THE CLAIM. A stacked scrim does not respond to pointer movement, and it never had to: the scrim is what PREVENTED the paint, and something else FORCED the repaint. g5 named only the first half, which is why it read as a story. THE SECOND HALF, read out of the stylesheet: app/globals.css:2828 .al-row:hover. The meeting rows inside the panel body carry a hover rule, so a pointer entering the panel triggers a style recalc on .al-row that invalidates paint INSIDE .al-overlay-body - the exact container whose pixels were missing. A committed rule, not a hypothesis, sitting precisely where the defect was. A phone has no hover, which is why a phone reader never got the free repair. WHY IT FAILED TO PAINT: two backdrop-filter surfaces stacked over the WebGL canvas - the state-focus scrim with the list overlay's own blur (.al-overlay, globals.css:2736) directly on top. g5's A/B distinguishes them: removing the OVERLAY's blur did nothing (0 of 4 at 390px, no better than control); removing the SCRIM underneath painted. WHAT THAT IS WORTH, as a bound rather than as green: 4 of 4 against a 25% failure rate happens 32% of the time and was correctly dismissed. 320 consecutive passes put the 95% UPPER BOUND ON THE FAILURE PROBABILITY AT 0.93%; if the old rate held, this result would occur about once in 10^40 runs. Item: walk:all compares check SETS, not two totals

Item: NAMED REGRESSION: zooming out to z7 at 85701 wipes every pin
Detail: pnpm walk:all reports 'pins 11 to 12 to 0 across zooms 11.0 to 9.0 to 7.0' at 85701. The g3 win behind CLAUDE.md's 'More viewport must never mean fewer pins' is undone at the widest zoom. 11 to 12 is correct; 12 to 0 is the defect.
Notes: FOUND 2026-08-18 (g13) by pnpm walk:all, which is exactly what that suite exists for - the check carries g3 as its shipping session so it printed as a named regression rather than an anonymous red line. DIAGNOSED HALFWAY, and the half that is settled is stated so the next session does not repeat it. THE SERVER IS NOT THE CAUSE, proven: /api/meetings at 85701's centre returns 89 meetings at radiusKm=25, 97 at 60, 97 at 150, and 97 at 400 (clamped to 150 and saying so in the response's own radiusKm). That is monotonic and correct at every rung, so lib/map/viewport-radius.ts and the ladder clamp are both behaving. THE DEFECT IS CLIENT-SIDE: the data is on the wire and the pins are not on screen. NOT DIAGNOSED, and deliberately not half-fixed under the deferral boundary: which client layer drops them. The probe counts entries whose element dataset.hidden is not 'true', so the two candidate shapes are (a) the pin pool marking every entry hidden at low zoom, or (b) the map effect's clip/mask - a known Chromium behaviour in this repo's own memory is that an OVERSIZED clip-path is dropped entirely, and projected geometry at z7 is far larger than at z11, so a mask that hides outside a region would hide everything the moment it is dropped or inverted. Reproduced 1 of 2 runs, both against production, minutes apart, same build. WHAT THAT RULES IN: a timing shape, not a geometry one - a deterministic clip-path or culling bound would fail every run. The likeliest candidate is now the settle re-query itself: the check zooms with __wtpZoomOut and waits a fixed 1600ms, so a slow /api/meetings answer at the widest rung could leave the pool emptied and not yet refilled at the instant the probe reads. WHAT IS STILL SETTLED: the server is innocent, on the evidence already in this row. DO NOT close this row on a green walk - one green run is exactly what the first re-run produced, and the walk check as written cannot tell a slow refill from a wipe. Give it the instrumentation above before ruling.|| CLOSED 2026-08-18 (g14, branch claude/g14-final-queue-0818). test 977 pass / 0 fail; lint 0 errors; tsc --noEmit clean. Item: Two scheduled workflows push to main with no rebase, so a collision loses a run
Detail: intake-tripwire.yml and refresh-meetings-snapshot.yml both commit and 'git push origin main' with no pull, rebase or retry. When both run close together the second push is rejected 'fetch first' and the job fails red after doing all of its work correctly.
Notes: FOUND 2026-08-18 (g13) while verifying R43 and R44: both workflows were dispatched at once to prove the two fixes, the tripwire pushed its report first, and the meetings refresh - whose ingest, whose M59 gate and whose commit had all SUCCEEDED - failed on the push alone. Re-dispatched by itself it passed, which is the proof the failure was the race and not the work. The scheduled cadences make this uncommon rather than impossible (17 past every sixth hour against 41 past ten), and a run lost this way is not silent - it goes red - so this is a P2. THE FIX IS SMALL AND SHOULD BE CONSIDERED WHOLE RATHER THAN PATCHED TWICE: a pull --rebase before the push, or a short retry loop, applied to BOTH workflows in one edit, since a fix on one only moves which job loses. Note the failure mode it must not create: a rebase that silently drops the commit would turn a red run into a green one that changed nothing, which is the empty success CLAUDE.md forbids - so the retry has to verify the push landed and stay red if it did not.

Item: walk:all reads a rendered outcome once after a fixed wait, in 33 more places
Detail: Three checks in scripts/walk-all.mts reported working surfaces as NAMED REGRESSIONS this session because they slept a fixed interval and then read the DOM once. A fixed wait plus a single read cannot tell GONE from NOT YET.
Notes: OPENED 2026-08-18 (g14) as the class behind three separate false reports in one session, all against the same build. (1) THE PIN FLOOR (R47): the zoom check slept 4000ms and read the pin count once, so a 200-500ms window at zero was caught on some runs and not others - reported as 'reproduced 1 of 2 runs, a race' when continuous sampling showed 4 of 4. (2) THE ASK REFUSAL (A07): slept 4500ms and read once; the classifier is a network round trip measured at 3190ms, 3171ms, 8397ms and 3166ms across the four zips, so whichever zip was slow that run failed. Walk 1 failed 85701 and 07866; a probe minutes later found those two fast and 85641 slow - proof it is a race and not per-zip behaviour. (3) THE A02 DIGEST: read the DOM with NO wait at all, at whatever moment the preceding geometry checks happened to finish. It passed the whole suite on one run and printed 'no digest rendered' at 85701 and 85641 on the next, twenty minutes later, about a digest that renders. ALL THREE ARE FIXED and each now waits for an OUTCOME rather than a duration - polling until the thing it is asking about has settled, then reading, with the read happening anyway at the ceiling so a genuine absence still fails on the truth. THE CLASS AUDIT, stated as a count rather than described: scripts/walk-all.mts contains 36 waitForTimeout calls. Three are converted. THE OTHER 33 ARE NOT AUDITED INDIVIDUALLY and that is stated rather than implied - most are legitimate settle waits after a navigation or a click rather than waits on a rendered outcome, and converting all of them blindly at the end of a session would be a large untested change to the one instrument every session depends on. WHAT THIS ROW IS: walk the remaining 33, decide for each whether it is waiting for a SETTLE (fine as it is) or for an OUTCOME (must poll), convert only the second kind, and state the split. THE TEST that a conversion is honest: it must never wait until the check PASSES. Waiting for an outcome means waiting until the surface has said something - a refusal or an answer, a count or a named gap - and then judging what it said. A poll that exits only on success would turn every one of these into a check that cannot fail, which is worse than the flake it replaces. WHY THIS IS A P2 AND NOT A P0: a false NAMED REGRESSION is loud, not silent - it costs a session's time and it erodes trust in the suite, but it never ships a wrong number to a reader. The direction of the error matters and it is the safe one. || RESOLVED FOR THE ASK FAMILY 2026-08-18 (g14), same session, and the class count is restated. THE FIX THAT HELD: every ask question gets a FRESH PAGE. There is no reliable way to tell a stale outcome from a new one on a page that already has one, so the page stops already having one - which is this repo own standing note about the per-zip loop applied rather than worked around. RESULT: pnpm walk:all against production 534f631 is 302 ok, 0 FAIL, 0 named regressions, with the ask checks settling consistently at 3.1-5.3s where they had been reporting 262ms and 2089ms. Item: sendBeacon bypasses the synthetic-run header, so our own automated runs land ORGANIC
Detail: lib/db/run-marker.ts declares a run through an HTTP header, and Playwright extraHTTPHeaders do not apply to navigator.sendBeacon. lib/log/client.ts PREFERS sendBeacon. Any event leaving by that path is recorded ORGANIC - our own robots counted as readers in the store we sell.
Notes: OPENED 2026-08-18 (g14), and it is opened because it BIT, not as a theory. THREE QUESTION_ASKED rows landed ORGANIC with run_id null at 2026-08-18T18:13:00Z, 18:14:12Z and 18:15:25Z, inside walk 7's window of 18:05:43Z to 18:16:18Z. They are ours. The exact window is recorded in docs/synthetic-runs.md so a correction is a filter and never a hunt. WHY IT SURFACED NOW rather than earlier: g14's fix for the ask checks reloads the page between questions, and a page unload is exactly when a queued beacon flushes. The hole was always there; the reload made it fire. That is worth stating because it means the row is about a LATENT hole in every browser script, not about the reload. FIXED FORWARD in 10 contexts - all 5 in scripts/walk-all.mts and 1 each in this session's five probe scripts (probe-r47, probe-m139, probe-a07, measure-load, shoot-ballot-pill) - by deleting navigator.sendBeacon in an addInitScript before the page loads, which forces the fetch fallback, and fetch DOES carry extraHTTPHeaders. THE COST IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: those runs no longer exercise the beacon transport at all. That is the right trade for now - a suite that pollutes the sold store on every run is worse than one that tests a transport one layer down - but it is a trade and a later session may prefer the other fix below. THE CLASS AUDIT, as a count: scripts/ holds 50 browser contexts. 10 are guarded. 40 ARE NOT, across 36 scripts - every tester-walk, every shoot, every measure, pairs, perf, overlap-audit, verify-sources-tab, walk-0815g, walk-r39, walk-r40 and walk-r41. Any of them run against production leaks the same way. WHAT THIS ROW IS: guard the remaining 40, and decide whether the guard is the right shape at all. THE ALTERNATIVE WORTH PRICING AT THE SAME TIME, because deleting a DOM method in every test is a workaround rather than a fix: teach the marker to travel in the BODY as well as the header. lib/log/client.ts already posts a JSON payload, so a run id read from a page-level global (planted by addInitScript) would ride inside it and survive both transports, and the route would trust the body only when the header is absent. That fixes the class once instead of once per script, and it would also cover any future transport. THE THREE ROWS ARE NOT BACKMARKED, deliberately: pnpm searchlog:backmark needs a write to production, and the only sanctioned write path is intake-limiter-purge (R43). Correcting them needs the author at the console or a new named sanction, and a session must not grant itself one. AUTHOR DECISION NEEDED on that correction; everything else here is ordinary work. || CORRECTED 2026-08-18 (g14), same session, and the correction is the point. THE FIRST FIX WAS A NO-OP: delete navigator.sendBeacon removes an OWN property, and sendBeacon lives on Navigator.prototype, so the method still resolved. It type-checked, it read correctly, and it changed nothing. Caught the only way it could be - by re-running the walk and checking a number that should not have moved. ORGANIC WENT 3 TO 7: four more of our own rows landed as readers in the very run meant to prove the fix. THE WORKING FORM, now in all ten contexts, is an explicit override: Object.defineProperty(navigator, "sendBeacon", { value: undefined, configurable: true }). VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT rather than by reading it again - organic before a run that asks three questions: 7; organic after: 7; synthetic across the same run 2143 to 2150, so the events landed declared. THE FULL LEAK IS SEVEN ROWS, all QUESTION_ASKED, all run_id null, in two windows: 18:13:00Z, 18:14:12Z, 18:15:25Z (walk 7) and 18:34:23Z, 18:35:32Z, 18:36:43Z, 18:37:52Z (walk 8). Still not backmarked, for the reason already stated - it needs a production write nobody has sanctioned.|| 2026-08-18 (g16, branch claude/g16-deploy-leaks-queue-0818). CLOSED AS A CLASS, NOT AS A CENSUS. THE CONSTRUCTION OF A BROWSER IS NOW ONE FUNCTION: scripts/browser.mts exports launchGuarded, and 45 scripts - every script in the tree that drives a browser - come through it. It applies three things at construction, so none of them can be forgotten: the run header on every context; the sendBeacon override, installed by addInitScript before the page's first script runs; and a run id MINTED FROM THE SCRIPT'S LABEL when the environment set none. That third one is new and it closes a hole nobody had named: syntheticRunHeaders() returns an empty object for an unset WTP_RUN_ID, and an empty object means ORGANIC, so a forgotten export was a silent total leak. launchGuarded refuses to open a browser at all if the marker comes out empty. So the leak is the UNLOAD-TIME beacon specifically, which is exactly why it surfaced when g14's ask checks started reloading the page between questions and not before. THE UNLOAD PATH IS FIXED AT THE SOURCE, and the workaround stays. The permanent plant is unchanged and still leaks, which is what makes the pass mean anything. THE DENOMINATOR, established rather than remembered (item 4a): 50 counted .newContext( CALL SITES in scripts/ before R50 and 45 counted the FILES holding them — both correct, different denominators, and the five that looked unaccounted for were never missing. Item: The MapLibre/application split is decorative, not a measurement
Detail: The client budget attributes a WHOLE chunk to MapLibre if the chunk's bytes contain the string maplibre. During AUD-03's re-chunking the split moved from 2155530 to 1148412 with no map code touched at all. The auditor asked for the two tracked apart so map cost cannot hide inside application cost, and a number that redraws itself when chunks are reshuffled cannot do that job.
Notes: 2026-08-18 (g18 item 3) BUILT as the real fix rather than the sanctioned fallback. scripts/attribute-client-bytes.mjs reads the build's own source maps, decodes the VLQ mappings, and attributes each run of generated bytes to the module that produced it - so it attributes WITHIN a chunk, and re-chunking cannot move it. PROVEN ON A REAL RE-CHUNK: DistrictPopup was moved from a next/dynamic boundary to a static import, no map code touched - substring 1149452 -> 1127962, a move of 21,490 bytes; provenance 873003 -> 872955, a move of 48 bytes (0.006%, minifier context shifting). The same plant is in tests/build-attribution.test.ts as a synthetic fixture, WITH the substring method asserted to FAIL it, so the new method passing proves something. WHAT THE OLD NUMBER GOT WRONG, now that both can be read: it put MapLibre at 43% of the initial JS; by provenance it is 32%. The gap is two chunks it credited whole - one of 1,096,720 bytes that is mostly but not only the library, and one of 51,533 bytes of application code that merely MENTIONS it. This session's own AUD-06 change was the tell: it touched application modules only, and applicationBytes read 1,568,189 across three builds while maplibreBytes absorbed the entire delta in both directions. THREE HONESTY CONSTRAINTS: unmapped bytes are their own bucket and are never folded into application; gzip is NOT split, because compression is not additive and the old per-side gzip figures were arithmetic on a number with no per-module meaning, so they are retired; and a missing map REFUSES - the check prints the substring figure labelled ESTIMATE ONLY, NOT MEASUREMENT and says how to measure it, rather than reporting a zero. The three buckets reconcile to the byte, asserted at measurement time, which caught the first cut counting UTF-16 columns against a UTF-8 total, 671 bytes out. Source maps are not shipped: next.config.ts emits them only under WTP_ATTRIBUTION_BUILD=1. claude/g18-manifest-places-attribution-0818; test 1049 pass 0 fail, lint 0 errors 12 allowlisted warnings, tsc --noEmit clean, build green.

Item: clerksboards parser reads past published month restrictions and exceptions
Detail: Three of Tucson's 27 wired Clerk boards publish a schedule the parser expands more broadly than the body wrote it. Board 40: '2nd Tuesday of each month September through May @ 6:00 p.m.' - the September-through-May restriction is ignored, so June, July and August sittings would be emitted. Boards 58 and 59: '1st Thursday of each month @ 9:00 a.m. (except January it will be 01/08/26 and July will be 07/09/26)' - the parenthetical exception is ignored, so those two months get the ordinary Nth-weekday date instead of the published one. Neither produces a wrong date inside today's serving window, because the recurrence loop only walks five months ahead from the window start; both will as soon as the window or the loop widens. This is one class, not three instances: the grammar has no representation for a restriction or an exception attached to a recurrence. Found 2026-08-18 (g19) by re-running the classification over all 56 board pages, and recorded rather than fixed under the addition rule.
Notes: Opened 2026-08-18 (g19 item 1b). The fix has a shape already: monthsInParens() in lib/sources/clerksboards/index.ts reads a month set out of a parenthetical for grammar C, and the same helper is what a restriction clause needs. The exception form is different - it is a date OVERRIDE for a named month, so the recurrence has to be expanded first and then patched, which is why it is not a one-line change. A test must assert the negative (no June/July/August date for board 40) as well as the positive, because the current window hides the defect and a test written against today's window would pass on a broken parser.

Related and already-standing: the refresh corollary (a failed fetch never silently empties a previously-full surface) is the same rule one layer up, and this is that rule applied to a SUCCESSFUL fetch that simply found less.
